steps: Meiosis produces haploid cells by reducing the chromosome number to half.
It maintains the constant chromosome number of a species from one generation to the next when fertilization restores the diploid number.
It produces genetic variation through crossing over and the independent assortment of chromosomes.
items.finalAnswer: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and creates genetic variation, helping maintain the chromosome number of a species across generations.

steps: Cell-cycle checkpoints normally control whether a cell can proceed to the next stage and help prevent the division of cells with damaged DNA.
If mistakes in these checkpoints allow abnormal cells to continue dividing, they may divide uncontrollably.
The resulting mass of abnormal cells may form a tumour and can lead to cancer.
items.finalAnswer: Faulty cell-cycle checkpoints can allow abnormal cells to divide uncontrollably, leading to tumour formation and cancer.

steps: Skin cells are continually lost or damaged, so they keep dividing to replace them and repair the tissue.
Nerve and muscle cells become highly specialised for their functions.
These specialised cells permanently leave the cell cycle and do not normally divide.
items.finalAnswer: Skin cells divide to replace lost or damaged cells, whereas specialised nerve and muscle cells permanently leave the cell cycle.
